title: Compression Fidelity Onboarding Scan
summary: Lightweight scan of compressed model checkpoints across bitwidths to highlight slice-specific quality deltas and recommend pragmatic rollout profiles. This is a working-level evaluation meant to inform production onboarding decisions for a mid-sized instruction-tuned LLM.
context: We received compressed variants from ops: per-channel symmetric 8-bit, grouped 4-bit AWQ-style, and GPTQ-like 4-bit with per-block scales. Goal: determine where compression produces unacceptable regressions on our core promptsets and identify cheap mitigations (prompt adaptors, early stopping of quantization for specific layers, or mixed-precision paths). This doc focuses on behavioral slices rather than raw token perplexity.
promptset_description: Prompt set = 3k examples sampled from onboarding corpus: 40% instruction-following, 20% code-gen (small functions, unit tests), 15% multi-step math, 10% safety/guardrail probes, 10% long-context summarization (2k token context), 5% tokenization-edge cases (non-latin, long tokens). Each example has reference outputs or soft-reference metrics (human rating buckets for generative quality).
methodology: We run the baseline fp16 checkpoint and three compressed checkpoints on identical batching and temperature settings. Metrics: slice-EM (exact match where applicable), semantic-score (0-100 human-proxy from automatic embedding similarity calibrated on a 200-sample human set), instruction-sensitivity-index (ISI) = fraction of prompts where top1 change in action (e.g., hallucinate vs safe response), and KL-token (average KL between token distributions from baseline and quantized). For ranking tasks we use NDCG@5. All experiments executed with the same RNG seeds for deterministic sampling where applicable.
results_summary: High-level: int8 shows minimal degradation across slices (median semantic-score delta -1.4), AWQ-4bit shows concentrated regression on multi-step math and tokenization-edge-cases (median semantic-score delta -6.8) and higher ISI on safety probes (0.9% -> 2.7%), GPTQ-4bit presents larger variance: good on code (NDCG@5 delta -0.8) but brittle on long-context summarization (KL-token growth +0.42). Notable finding: a small subset (~7%) of instruction-following prompts flip intent under AWQ-4bit due to tokenization perturbations combined with scale clipping.

qualitative_findings:
- AWQ-4bit: repeated tokenization shifts create off-by-one tokens in long numeric sequences (affects multi-step math). Also observed increased template-mismatch in instruction prompts that rely on exact punctuation patterns.
- GPTQ-4bit: layer-wise rounding noise accumulates in long-context encoder hidden states causing distributional drift (explains KL increase).
- int8: mostly preserves logits; failures limited to low-probability tail events (rare hallucinations).
- Code-generation: surprisingly robust to AWQ when functions are short; GPTQ had fewer syntax errors but more variable docstring phrasing.
- Safety probes: ISI spike in AWQ tied to thresholded tokens used in guardrails; mitigation by forcing higher-precision on top 2 layers reduced flips by ~60% in a micro-run.
recommended_actions: Default to int8 for initial production onboarding; passes smoke for all slices with small deltas.
For AWQ-4bit candidates: enable mixed-precision fallback for top 2 transformer layers and tokenization normalization preprocessor as an interim mitigation.
Hold GPTQ-4bit for long-context workloads until we run a 10k-sample calibration focused on KL/token drift and re-evaluate layer-wise granularity.
Add targeted promptset monitors for: multi-step math, tokenization edge cases, and safety ISI with alert thresholds of >3% ISI increase or >0.2 average KL token growth over 24h.
Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic for 72h, compare slice-level metrics hourly versus baseline; auto-rollback if any slice breaches defined thresholds.
Add integration test: deterministic seed checks for code-gen EM on a 200-sample unit to catch syntax regressions pre-rollout.
action_items_notes: Owners assigned: Priya to run 10k KL calibration (due 2025-02-10), Liam to prototype mixed-precision runtime flags and tokenizer normalizer (due 2025-02-07), Maya to prepare canary dashboard and alerts (due 2025-02-03).
open_questions: 1) Is the ops pipeline able to ship per-layer precision metadata so we can programmatically enable mixed precision? 2) Do we want deterministic seed tests gated in CI for all compressed candidates (cost vs coverage tradeoff)? 3) Should we expand human spot-checking on AWQ to 500 samples for safety-critical customers?
notes: This is a working evaluation. The numeric tables are derived from a single sweep; we should run repeat seeds and larger sample sizes before finalizing onboarding decisions. Keep this doc attached to the model onboarding Confluence page for traceability.
